descriptionChirho: Desirableness, preciousness, or costly treasures. Used both of persons and things: of Daniel as a 'man of treasures' (ish chamudot), i.e., one greatly treasured or beloved by God (Dan 9:23, 10:11, 10:19), of precious goods and costly items plundered or hoarded (2 Chr 20:25, 'precious things'; Dan 11:38, 'with treasures'; Dan 11:43, 'treasures of gold and silver'). The plural form chamudot functions as an abstract noun of quality indicating high value and desirability.

Choice or desirable food, delicacies. Used specifically of Daniel's abstention from rich food during his three-week mourning period: 'I ate no delicacies' (lechem chamudot, literally 'bread of desirablenesses,' Dan 10:3). This specialized culinary sense refers to luxurious or pleasurable foods that one might forgo during fasting or mourning, distinct from the more general sense of 'precious things' or 'treasures.'
